brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: One Hex base (piece:0,0,0) with a Keyhole hanger (hex-acc-keyhole) bolted on face slot 0, the wall-side face, so it hangs on screws already in a wall. Configurator check: meshClash clear, no rule errors.

Three Hook plates (hex-acc-hook, each with two hooks) on faces slots 2, 3 and 4, giving six hooks on the front of the rack. The hooks are physical and placed, but the catalog offers no hand-tool prop that hangs on them (hooks only take a cable coil, gaffer tape or FPV goggles), so no tools are staged on the hooks.

requirements.requirement: Material, strength and load suitability for holding tools on a wall
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only; it cannot verify printed-material strength, load rating or wall-fixing adequacy. Two faces (slots at 30 and 270 degrees) are still open; the house cap and joint-lock ops made no change.

finish.summary: Built a single-cell wall-mounted tool rack: one Hex base with a keyhole hanger on the wall face and three hook plates (six hooks) on the front faces. The build checks clear of mesh clashes. Hand tools are not staged as props because hooks accept only cable coils, gaffer tape or goggles. Strength and wall-fixing are outside what the configurator can verify.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Hook plate
